forecasts.question: Will Iran resume negotiations with the US before EOD 2026-06-16?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED AMBIGUOUS: No confirmed publicly held negotiating session before EOD June 16. Pakistan PM Sharif finalized MOU language via back-channel relay June 14; Witkoff and Araghchi traveled to Switzerland June 19 for formal talks convened June 21-22 — both events fall after the June 16 deadline. MOU finalization via relay does not constitute a held session under the ambiguity rule (relay of written messages = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO). RESOLVED-AMBIGUOUS.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if, before EOD 2026-06-16, a publicly confirmed HELD negotiating session (direct or mediated via Oman/Qatar/Pakistan) occurs between named US and Iranian principals/envoys, OR an official Iranian statement rescinds the 2026-06-01 suspension.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR one TIER1 + official Iranian state-media; State Dept or Iran MFA statement also resolves.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Trump-only assertions without Iranian/mediator confirmation do NOT count; written-message exchanges that are not a convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO; one side asserting talks continue without a named convened session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a publicly confirmed direct Israel-Iran military exchange — Israeli strikes on Iranian targets AND Iranian strikes on Israeli/Israeli-claimed targets — within any rolling 48h window between 2026-06-10 and 2026-06-24.

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu's coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: RESOLVED AMBIGUOUS: The Knesset voted 62-0 on July 17, 2026, with all coalition members voting for dissolution — the coalition never fell below 61 seats (no majority loss). Election set to October 27, 2026 (not earlier than Oct 27). Neither resolution criterion technically triggered: criterion 1 (coalition loss of majority) is explicitly not met — the 62-0 vote means coalition retained full voting bloc; criterion 2 (election date earlier than Oct 27) is not met — the date is exactly Oct 27. Sunday cold-start: Analyst p_cold=0.97 (gap 62pp from inherited 0.35) based on UTJ/Shas exit claims. Judge rejects this cold-start reassessment: the 62-0 vote is the controlling public record; claims of UTJ/Shas departure that preceded the vote are contradicted by their participation in a unanimous dissolution vote. RESOLVED-AMBIGUOUS. Successor forecast: F4 (new board), Likud bloc 61 seats Oct 27.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If coalition votes for own dissolution while retaining 61+: AMBIGUOUS. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays).

forecasts.question: Will an IAEA inspection team conduct an on-site visit at Fordow or Natanz before EOD 2026-08-19?
forecasts.delta_reason: New near-term forecast. VP Vance stated June 22 that Iran had agreed to IAEA inspections as part of the Switzerland roadmap's monitoring working group. The MOU collapsed July 8, removing the formal framework. Iran's Foreign Ministry stated August 12 that inspection access remains contingent on a final binding agreement — not a roadmap. IAEA Deputy DG for Safeguards Massimo Aparo told Reuters August 14 that monitoring capabilities remain significantly degraded and provisional June 22 arrangements have not been operationalized. No IAEA press release has confirmed any Fordow or Natanz site visits since June. P set at 0.20 reflecting near-absence of preconditions for a breakthrough in a 3-day window.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if an IAEA press statement or Director General communication confirms IAEA inspectors conducted an on-site visit at Fordow (underground enrichment facility) or Natanz (main enrichment complex) at any point between 2026-08-16 and EOD 2026-08-19.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: IAEA official press release or Director General statement, confirmed by Reuters/AP/AFP. Iranian state media claims of IAEA access alone do NOT resolve without an IAEA official statement.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: IAEA inspectors permitted to travel to Iran but denied Fordow/Natanz site access = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Inspections of non-enrichment sites do NOT count. IAEA verbal assurances without a published access report = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

indicators.name: IAEA Director General confirms inspectors have entered Fordow or Natanz

forecasts.question: Will the US Treasury renew or extend General License X (covering Iranian crude oil, petrochemical products, and petroleum products) beyond its August 21, 2026 expiry, before EOD 2026-08-21?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. OFAC General License X was issued June 22-23 as part of the Switzerland roadmap's 60-day sanctions relief tranche, expiring August 21. No Federal Register notice of renewal as of August 16. Trump's August 14 Hormuz territorial declaration and the August 15 UAE vessel attack introduce adversarial signaling that may reduce a quiet renewal's domestic political palatability. However, a non-renewal removes Iran's primary remaining financial incentive for the Oman channel and eliminates the US's principal economic-leverage tool — the extension remains in the US's structural interest even under adversarial posture. Named US Treasury officials declined to comment on renewal status (Bloomberg, August 14). No White House statement as of August 16.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if OFAC issues a new or amended general license extending sanctions relief on Iranian-origin crude oil, petrochemical products, or petroleum products beyond August 21, 2026, before EOD August 21.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: OFAC Federal Register notice OR Reuters/AP/Bloomberg reporting a named Treasury or OFAC official confirming the extension. A presidential statement alone without an accompanying OFAC instrument does NOT resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: A Trump social-media assertion without an OFAC legal instrument does NOT count. A conditional extension requiring new Iranian compliance steps before taking effect = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Partial extension covering some but not all previously licensed product categories = AMBIGUOUS — resolve as YES only if crude oil coverage is explicitly extended.

indicators.name: OFAC Federal Register notice published extending General License X
Named US Treasury or State Dept official publicly confirms intention to extend

forecasts.question: Will a formal Iran-Oman-US framework for Hormuz commercial transit management — specifying a transit protocol not contingent solely on Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority (PGSA) permit authority — be publicly announced before EOD 2026-09-15?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. Iran-Oman negotiations described as in final stages August 2; Iran set steep conditions August 8 (US acknowledgment of June MOU violation, full secondary-sanctions removal as precondition, IRGC veto over any Hormuz access protocol). Oman FM Albusaidi-Araghchi call August 12 produced no joint communiqué. Bloomberg source August 12: talks not close to a framework. Trump's August 14 Hormuz territorial declaration and the August 15 UAE vessel attack directly undercut Oman's mediation framework. Three prior ceasefire cycles (April, June 17, June 23) collapsed within weeks. DA structural analysis accepted: PGSA permit authority creates a YES/NO definitional trap; Araghchi's divided mandate risks disavowal. P set at 0.22.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a jointly announced Iran-Oman-US or Oman-mediated framework for Hormuz commercial transit is published by Oman's Foreign Ministry or confirmed by named US AND Iranian principals — specifying that commercial vessels may transit Hormuz under a mutually recognized protocol not solely governed by unilateral Iranian PGSA permit authority — before EOD 2026-09-15.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Reuters/AP/AFP/Bloomberg OR official Oman MFA statement confirmed by one additional TIER1. Trump-only or Iranian FM-only assertions without the other side's confirmation do NOT qualify.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: An Iranian 'willingness to negotiate' statement, Oman FM 'positive atmosphere' readout, or Bloomberg 'close to deal' report without a jointly announced framework = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A PGSA-permit-only system does NOT count as a mutually recognized open Hormuz. Any framework announced then disavowed within 48h by a named Iranian official above the rank of spokesperson = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO.

Iran MFA statement explicitly acknowledges a transit framework not subject to unilateral PGSA permits

forecasts.question: Will Israeli forces conduct a TIER1-confirmed airstrike on targets physically located inside Iranian territory (within Iran's internationally recognized borders) before EOD 2026-09-30?
forecasts.delta_reason: New forecast. The June 2026 ceasefire collapsed July 8; Israel-Hezbollah exchanges in Lebanon resumed and escalated through August. IDF conducted its deadliest Lebanon strikes since late June on August 15 (11+ killed, Radwan Force commander killed per Al Jazeera/Times of Israel). Iran struck a UAE oil vessel in Hormuz on August 15 and has attacked shipping repeatedly. Trump's August 14 Hormuz territorial claim changes US strategic posture. Prior base rate: two rounds of direct Israel-Iran strikes occurred in this conflict cycle (Twelve-Day War Feb 2026; June 13-14 exchange). The 45-day window is long enough to capture at least one significant escalation event if Hormuz crisis deepens. P set near even reflecting the conflict's active trajectory.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if two independent TIER1 sources (Reuters/AP/AFP/CNN/Al Jazeera) OR one TIER1 plus an official IDF statement confirm Israeli airstrikes on targets physically located inside Iran's internationally recognized land borders between 2026-08-16 and 2026-09-30.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 OR IDF statement + one TIER1. IRGC or Iranian state media statement alone does NOT resolve — Iranian military communiqués have been contradicted by TIER1 in this conflict.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Israeli strikes in Lebanon, Syria, Iraq, or international waters against IRGC-linked targets do NOT count — must be strikes physically inside Iranian territory. Strikes on Iranian-flagged vessels in international waters do NOT count. Israeli strikes on Iranian proxies operating from non-Iranian soil do NOT count.
